name: Bullet

team.summary: Adi and Alex, fresh out of working at AppLovin and Citadel, started Bullet in a senior year dorm after going through six pivots including an AI hedge fund and browser-use agent.

product.summary: Bullet is a faster coding agent and harness providing model routing, targeted search, aggressive context hygiene, and efficient parallel execution, claiming 95.8% resolution on SWE-bench Verified.

market.summary: Developers and engineers using AI coding agents who suffer from slow execution speeds and latency from tools like Claude Code and Codex.

risks.risk: Frequent pivots prior to this project raise sustainability and conviction questions.
Closed-source proprietary binary with high permission requirements (root/exec) raises supply chain security and trust concerns.
Harness defensibility is low as users can replicate routing and prompt strategies in open tools.

founder_depth.why: Technical backgrounds at AppLovin and Citadel, shipping in public, built out of personal frustration.

shipping_evidence.why: Shipped desktop downloads, CLI via npm, video demo, and documented benchmark results.

demand_signal.why: Strong community engagement with 121 points and 89 comments on HN, though accompanied by critical user feedback.

defensibility.why: It is a closed-source harness wrapping existing model APIs; users note it can easily be cloned or replicated via prompts and MCPs.

analysis.verdict_reason: Low defensibility for an AI coding harness combined with proprietary binary distribution security concerns make this off-thesis for long-term venture infrastructure.
would_change_my_mind: Open-sourcing the core codebase for security auditability
Proving sustainable enterprise monetization beyond a wrapper harness
Demonstrating compounding technical moats that cannot be replicated via prompt engineering or MCPs
data_gaps: Exact proprietary IP details beyond wrapper/routing logic
